page0.text:
...I can't bring it down.
My hands holding the dagger keep trembling, and I can't stab Saber in the chest.

page1.text:
...
She just keeps staring at me.
She's gazing at me without any particular emotion, like someone watching firelight on the opposite shore.

page2.text:
It was only a few days.
Less than eight days have passed since the night I lost her.
...No, I guess it's already been that long.
It's been that long since I lost her vivid golden hair and gentle green eyes.

page3.text:
The beauty of her whirling swordsmanship and silver armor is still fresh in my mind.
She accepted an ignorant boy as her Master and served as my sword until the end.
No matter how many times she was hurt or faced death,
her conviction never dulled for a moment.

page4.text:
I won't forget her.
I can't possibly forget the miracle of that night.
Her golden hair drenched in moonlight.
That was...
That was an eternal sight that will never be lost, no matter how much she changes.

page5.text:
...
Then, I understand.
I can't kill Saber.
Even though she's a shadow of her former self covered in sinister magical energy, she's still the Saber who protected me.
How could I possibly kill her?

page6.text:
"Sa...ber..."
...I drop the dagger.
It plunges not into her chest, but the dry earth.

page7.text:
"..."
...The black swordsman says nothing.
Her gradually healing body is already fully restored.
...Her Master's magical energy must be enormous.
She's recovered all the power she spent, on top of her injuries.

page8.text:
"...Shirou, this is the first time I have hated you."
I understand her hatred.
"You're telling me to kill you."
It's only natural she'd be disappointed.

page9.text:
"Very well.
I will take your head, as you wish..."
The cave rumbles.
What's happening on the other side of the darkness?
A vibration that feels like death throes comes from the depths where Tohsaka went.

page10.text:
They remind me of someone wailing.
Is whoever's making these vibrations desperately calling for help...?

page11.text:
"Saber!?"
Saber sinks into the ground. It must be related.
No, her shadow devours her body.

page12.text:
"Saber, take my hand...!"
"I am delaying your execution. Sakura requests my aid."

page13.text:
"Guh...!"
...The shadow fades away.
It swallowed Saber whole and seeped away into the ground.

page17.text:
"...Rgh."
I suddenly wake up.
I was sleeping on my knees in a place I don't recognize.

page18.text:
"..."
...No, something's wrong.
Something's wrong, but I can't remember what no matter how hard I try.

page19.text:
"Hah, guh..."
I stand up.
I shake my head to clear it.
"...Oh, right. I need to head inside."
I seem to recall giving up something important to eliminate something else that was important to me.

page20.text:
"The dagger... I need to bring the dagger."
I pick up the Azoth Blade sticking out of the ground.
It's strange.
I was just holding it. So why is it in the ground now?

page21.text:
"......Gurgh."
I tightly fasten the bindings on my left arm.
I've used up most of my magical energy.
There's some left in Archer's arm, and some left in me.
I think I can manage with that combined power, but I'm limited to one last Projection. I won't be able to control Archer's arm anymore, no matter what I do afterwards.

page22.text:
"......"
...I'm forgetting something.
I'm forgetting something, but I need to hurry on.
My body feels hard.
I feel like I'm turning into a tin man.

page23.text:
...Someone is calling me from afar.
Their voice is...
unfamiliar.
It feels important to me. I walk on in my tin body.

page24.text:
After some time, I exit the cave.
The vibrations have already stopped.
An unpleasantly lukewarm, nauseating wind blows.

page25.text:
...
My left arm hurts.
With each step, something carves away my brain's ability to think, like a collapsing building.

page26.text:
I leave the black darkness and emerge into white darkness.
...My body is hot.
My body feels like a crucible thrust into a blast furnace. I'm dizzy.

page27.text:
The headache doubles.
My breath is hot, and the air is hotter.
The heat is fierce enough to scorch my skin, and the air feels rotten and traps in my throat.
I was wrong.
This is more like being in a creature's intestines than a furnace.

page28.text:
...
This is the final stage.
The final destination where Sakura is trapped, where Zouken lurks, where Tohsaka was headed.
But it's too quiet.
There are no signs of any fighting.
The white smoke prevents me from seeing Zouken's laughter, Tohsaka's trail, Sakura's gloomy face.

page29.text:
...
I walk forward before I can think about what might've happened.
I don't have the time or energy for it.
My mind only has a limited number of cycles left.
I have one Projection remaining.
I can't allow any excess considerations to degrade my final weapon.

page30.text:
I go up the cliff.
I single-mindedly climb the rocks, trying not to think of anything else.
There's a pillar of light resembling a black sun.
There...
is the dark, transformed Sakura.

page31.text:
"...Sakura."
"Hm?"
Sakura looks at me in wonder. In truly genuine amazement.
Her red eyes lack any emotion.

page32.text:
"......Sa—"
Their coldness is like a knife in the chest, and I can't even form words.
This was too foolish.
I've made the same mistake by being here as I did that other time.

page33.text:
"Oh, you came for me, Senpai. You took such a long time, I wondered if you ran away.
I'm sorry. I'll call myself back right now, okay?
I thought I'd give you a surprise by putting them all at the entrance. My mistake!"

page34.text:
She giggles.
Instantly, my spine freezes.
Sakura's smile is so unlike herself that I forget what I was going to say or what I needed to Project.

page35.text:
"...Sakura. Where's Tohsaka?"
I ask a stupid question.
I forget what I needed to say to bring Sakura back, and ask an unnecessary question that I already know the answer to.

page36.text:
"Huh...? You mean Nee-san?"
She looks confused, but not at my question.
It's as if she's disappointed that I don't know.

page37.text:
"Yeah. Tohsaka came here ahead of me. Where'd she go?"
"..."

page38.text:
The air is hot.
I imagine the wind melting my body.

page39.text:
From the cliff, I look out over the cave.
I don't see Tohsaka below.
The only signs of life are on top of this cliff.
At Sakura's feet...
There's something that looks like a black ribbon on the darkened ground around her feet.

page40.text:
I don't feel Tohsaka's presence.
I don't see her body.
I don't even see her bloodstains.

page41.text:
"Sakura, you..."
"It's just like you think, Senpai. Nee-san isn't in this world anymore.
I mean, I just swallowed her up earlier."

page42.text:
Who?
"Oh, of course, I didn't make a mess of her.
I made sure to eat her all up, body and mind. Even in this state, I'm still very polite."

page43.text:
Who?
"But Nee-san isn't dead. Even now, she's still suffering inside me.
...Hehe. She was so weak, you know. I'm making her experience everything that happened to me from the beginning. She broke down crying on the first day."

page44.text:
"Can you hear her? She keeps screaming 'help me,' 'I'm sorry,' just like I used to.
Ah... She's so adorable. She's even saying 'please, Sakura, let me out.'
Stupid Nee-san. Saying that makes me want to enjoy it even more."

page45.text:
Who?
"Hehe. She's so delicious I forgot myself.
Thank you for the meal, Senpai. You brought me the most delicious appetizer."

page46.text:
Who the hell is this?
My remaining thoughts go haywire.
My intellect bursts and scatters, and I don't know what I'm supposed to do or whom I'm even looking at.

page47.text:
"Sakura, you..."
You've gone too far for me to ever take you back.

page48.text:
"Stop it. Don't look at me like that.
...You've been very naughty too, you know. Nee-san couldn't kill me because you tried to save Saber.
If you hadn't done that, I would've been the one who died."

page49.text:
...
"But I'm so happy. You saved Saber, saved me, and killed Nee-san for me.
So..."

page51.text:
"I'm going to swallow you up, too.
Come on, Senpai. Nee-san's waiting for you."

page52.text: "Silly Nee-san. She started begging you for help. I'll put you right next to her, where you can even hold hands."

page53.text:
Shadows fall.
The light from the pillar is cut off, as if by some great wall.

page54.text:
Black shadows seethe out of the ground.
I don't know where they came from, but the giants surround me like a cage.

page55.text:
...
There's no escape.
The giants meld together and swallow me like a tsunami.
